about.title: Manhattan Beach Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Manhattan Beach sees a steady flow of traffic where beach visitors, commuters, and residents converge on corridors like Sepulveda Boulevard, Manhattan Beach Boulevard, Highland Avenue, and Rosecrans Avenue. Public records show 102 injury collisions and 133 people hurt in the most recent full year, with Tuesday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up often in reported crashes. Whether you were rear-ended near a Sepulveda intersection or sideswiped merging onto Rosecrans, the aftermath usually means insurance calls, medical appointments, and missed work all at once. We help injured drivers, passengers, cyclists, and pedestrians evaluate the crash, deal with the insurance company, and understand your options under California law. There's no cost to talk with us and no pressure to move forward until you're ready.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Statute of Limitations Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity (like the City of Manhattan Beach) may be responsible. Waiting to sort this out can quietly cost you your right to recover.

items.title: Pure Comparative Fault Rewards Careful Documentation
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you were partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces your payout. We can help preserve dashcam footage, photos, and witness statements from busy corridors like Highland Avenue before that evidence disappears.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement early — before you know the full extent of your injuries. Speaking with us first, on a contingency basis with no upfront fee, helps make sure nothing you say gets used to minimize your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Manhattan Beach?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a city vehicle or a hazard on a public road, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth getting a quick review sooner rather than later.

items.question: I was hit near Sepulveda or Rosecrans and I'm not sure who was at fault. Does that matter?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you share some blame for the crash. Your compensation would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, which is why documenting the scene and gathering witness accounts near busy corridors matters.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney, since insurers sometimes use early statements to downplay claims. Our team can advise you on this at no cost, and we only get paid if you recover compensation.
